# Provenance by Course

<!-- GENERATED by tools/gen_provenance.py -- do not hand-edit; re-run it instead.
     Every field is read from the build artifacts (laz/ tile names, dem_hd metadata, osm_geom.json,

     Verify with: python3 tools/gen_provenance.py --check -->

Exactly what data built each book. "Distributed" = built from open, public-domain and factual inputs
only, and handed out on that basis; "Personal" = do not distribute. This records what the build DID; it
is not legal advice and states no legal conclusion.

**Every book on this list is built only from:** OpenStreetMap geometry (ODbL 1.0), slope/contours
computed by us from public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR, par/yardage/handicap **facts** from published
scorecards, and — where an aerial or a missing green is needed — public-domain USDA NAIP.
No Esri/Maxar, Google, Apple or Bing imagery, and nothing from any commercial green-reading product.

**Flight dates are decoded from the LiDAR point records** (`tools/lidar_dates.py`), not from the
project name. Four courses were mislabelled by 2–12 years before this was measured, so the dataset
names below are taken from the actual tile filenames on disk.

**Geometry carries a date for the same reason.** Each row's OSM *extract* date is the earliest
`osm3s.timestamp_osm_base` across that course's Overpass responses — the instant of the planet data
they were computed from, read off the files rather than recorded by hand. The flight date lets a reader
judge whether the green SLOPE is current; without this one they cannot judge the same thing about the
hole and green SHAPES, and a re-bunkered hole looks exactly as authoritative as a current one.

## Notes on the special cases
- **Seamless-mosaic fallback.** A few greens have no usable LiDAR ground returns — bayside holes over
  water, or greens under heavy canopy. Those use the USGS **3DEP seamless DEM service** instead of the
  0.4 m point cloud: still public domain, just less sharp. That service is a MULTI-RESOLUTION MOSAIC, so its sampling is not its resolution: at every green this project has taken from it, the tier that answered carries a source cell of **2.70–2.73 m E-W × 3.42–3.43 m N-S** — 3DEP's 1/9 arc-second tier at these latitudes. This record and the cards both called it *1 m* until it was measured out of the arrays themselves (`render_green.source_lattice`, no network needed); that was an overstatement of about 9x in area, and the cards now print the measured cell instead of a tier. Separately, **no acquisition date for that raster is recorded anywhere in this build** — `tools/lidar_dates.py` decodes flight dates from LAZ point records and this path has no point cloud — so a row's flight date covers its 0.4 m greens only, and the cards say so.
- **Holes that print no height.** Every row above counts three things separately, and they are not the
  same thing: cards that PRINT a tee-to-green height, holes that were MEASURED, and holes that were
  never measured at all. A measured change under **3 ft** is suppressed as level
  (`generate.py`, `elev_phrase`), because the two independent sources that figure was checked against
  disagree by more than that on some holes — so a measurement is not a printed number.
  Across this corpus **186 measured holes print on 126 of 216 cards**.
  `fetch_hole_elev.py` declines to measure a hole at all when any of these holds: the hole has no mapped
  centreline; its mapped line neither spans the card yardage nor belongs to a straight par 3, so the back
  tee cannot be placed; there is **no usable green surface**; the tee sample holds too few ground
  returns; the mapped tee pad spans more height than `MAX_TEE_RELIEF_FT`, so a median over it does not
  stand for a tee height; or the change exceeds `MAX_PLAUSIBLE_FT` and can only be a units or datum
  fault. **Which of those applied to a given hole is printed in that stage's run log and is not written
  into `hole_elev.json`**, which records only the holes that got a figure — so the rows above do not
  attribute an individual omission and this record will not guess one. Earlier wording did guess: it told
  the reader that every hole without a height had a tee that could not be found or had no ground returns,
  on four courses where that was not the reason.
- **Hand-added greens.** Where OSM mapped no green at all, the putting surface was traced from
  **public-domain USDA NAIP** imagery and tagged `_digitized`. Only coordinates are derived; no
  imagery is embedded in any book. `fetch_osm.py` refuses to overwrite a cache it cannot read, so a
  re-fetch cannot silently delete this geometry.
- **Greens rebuilt after the flight.** Where a course was reconstructed after its LiDAR was flown,
  the map is real measured data but may no longer match the ground. Those cards are labelled
  *pre-rebuild data* and the guide page names the holes.
- **Yardage mode.** Where no trustworthy post-construction elevation exists at all, the book prints
  verified yardages with **blank greens** rather than slope maps that could be wrong.
- **Jay Blasi routing diagram (Poppy Ridge):** only **viewed**, to establish hole numbering; never
  reproduced or embedded. Extracting factual hole positions is not copying.

### Micke Grove Golf Links
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR (San Joaquin County, public domain)
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
- **rating** — Blue/White ratings/slopes are the card's MEN's values. Red publishes NEITHER here: the card's 70.0/116 under Red is the WOMEN's pair and both halves are withheld, so the tees card prints an em-dash for its rating and its slope.
- **scorecard** — Official Micke Grove Golf Links printed scorecard (mickegrove.com/course-details image attachment-1): Blue/White/Red per-hole yardages, par & men's handicap transcribed directly; all three tee totals verified (6565/6026/5286, par 72). NOTE: the official card's own hole numbering is authoritative for the nines. Blue/White ratings/slopes are the card's MEN's values. RED RATING AND SLOPE BOTH LEFT BLANK ON PURPOSE: the card's 70.0/116 under Red is one WOMEN's pair (the row beneath it is labelled 'Ladies' Handicap'); a 5286-yd tee cannot rate 70.0 where 6026 rates 68.5, and the card publishes no men's Red rating or slope. Printing the rating would inflate a boy's handicap differential by ~5 strokes. The 116 is the other half of that same women's pair, so it is withheld with it: a course handicap is index x slope / 113, the two rows above it are men's slopes (126, 122), and 116 sits almost exactly on their extrapolation to 5286 yd -- which is why it read as men's for as long as it did.
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_FEMALevee_D23 (2023), NAD83(2011) UTM10N + NAVD88; 0.4 m green surfaces at ~9-15 pts/m^2. All 18 holes mapped in OSM (no digitizing needed).

### Trump National Golf Club — Los Angeles
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR (public domain), project CA_LosAngeles_B23, flown 2023-10-02 (decoded from the point records by tools/lidar_dates.py, not from the project name). Ground-return density over the 18 greens RANGES from 10.4 to 15.3 points/m^2 (median 14.7); holes 10, 13 and 15 sit at the low end, 10.4-10.5, about 29% under the median, so a single figure would be stated more definitely than the data supports. Chosen over the two 2016 Los Angeles projects deliberately: 2023 is the newest dense survey covering this property.
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
- **rating** — Course ratings and slopes for all five tees are the USGA NCRDB men's values (CourseID 2594), which state gender explicitly: Black 75.0/144, Blue 72.3/137, White 70.2/131, Red 67.5/124, Gold 63.9/115. All five men's pairs are published, so no rating or slope is withheld here. Ratings fall monotonically with yardage (215.6 / 224.3 / 207.0 / 211.7 yd per rating stroke between adjacent tees), which is the arithmetic the club's own 2012 card fails.
- **scorecard** — Par, per-hole men's handicap and per-hole yardages for all five tees (Black/Blue/White/Red/Gold) are facts from the published scorecard. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS RECORD CLAIMED A SECOND, INDEPENDENT PUBLISHED CARD BEHIND THEM, AND THERE IS NOT ONE: the two places those figures were read are one publication on one host serving one table, so the claim is WITHDRAWN rather than reworded. A cross-check that did not happen is worse than none, because it is the reason nobody looks again. What does stand behind these numbers is arithmetic and open data. Every tee reconciles per-hole to its published out/in/total exactly: Black 3657/3214/6871, Blue 3347/2942/6289, White 3092/2726/5818, Red 2763/2496/5259, Gold 2362/2135/4497; par 36/35 = 71. Per-hole par is INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by OpenStreetMap's own golf=hole par tags, which agree on all 18 holes, and the per-hole YARDAGES are independently corroborated by measurement off the OSM centrelines and mapped tee pads -- see the yardage entry, which is the second opinion this record used to claim falsely and now has for real. Hole 11 is a 223 yd PAR 3 (it was a 302 yd par 4 before the 2006 re-routing; any source showing par 4 there is stale) and hole 18 is a 503 yd PAR 4 (unusual, but consistent across every source consulted) -- both printed as found. Men's stroke index 11,15,13,17,3,5,9,7,1 / 10,8,12,4,6,16,18,14,2; a women's index is published too (7,1,13,17,9,11,5,15,3 / 10,12,4,8,2,16,14,18,6) but this book prints the men's, as the guide card states. THE COURSE'S OWN 2012 PRINTED CARD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT USED: its Black row fails its own rating arithmetic (differenced against the tee below it, 328 yd per stroke of Course Rating, outside the 130-300 band tests/test_r17_yardage.py enforces), its slopes are stale, and it stacks the WOMEN'S ratings under Red and Gold so they read as men's -- the exact defect that shipped on micke-grove and had to be withdrawn. THE BAR THIS RECORD ONCE PUBLISHED FOR THAT TEST -- "a normal 190-265" -- WAS A FIGURE FROM NOWHERE, and it is retired. Measured over all 45 adjacent rated tee pairs in this corpus the real spread runs 141.8 to 284.0, so five pairs of published men's figures fell OUTSIDE the retired bar, and a bar this project's own books break is not a bar. The rejection of the 2012 back row stands on its own; only the bar it was judged against moved, and a test now derives that bar from the corpus instead of quoting it.
- **yardage** — MEASURED against the ground, not only transcribed. Two published back-tee sets circulate for this course and they differ on nearly every hole (6871 against 7240 total, with holes 5, 10, 14 and 17 apart by 46, 102, 70 and 39 yd), so the set this book prints was checked using ONLY open data already on disk: OpenStreetMap's 18 hole centrelines, 20 greens and 86 mapped tee polygons (ODbL), plus public-domain USGS 3DEP LiDAR ground returns. METHOD. Each centreline is bound to its green by geo.match_green and the green's area centroid is the target. No OSM tee pad here carries a colour or a ref, so pads are assigned to holes two independent ways and the two are compared: by OSM way-id band (this course was drawn hole by hole, so a hole's ways occupy a contiguous id band ending at that hole's green) and by line-of-play geometry (perpendicular offset from the hole's axis, with the along-track term deliberately SYMMETRIC in sign so the assignment has no preference for a pad sitting at the line start over one sitting behind it -- a cost that penalised negative offsets would have assumed away the very confound being tested). 78 of 86 pads agree outright; the 8 that disagree are resolved individually, and in every case one of the two readings is absurd on its face (a 941 yd par 5, a 420 yd par 3). The played distance then runs pad -> the next centreline vertex -> along the line -> the green centre, which is how a yardage is defined on a dogleg, on WGS84 geodesics through geo.mlat/geo.mlon. RESULT: the printed set is the one the ground supports, and the agreement is across ALL FIVE TEE ROWS rather than the back one alone -- 88 of the 90 card cells (5 tees x 18 holes) are matched by a mapped pad within 15 yd, median residual +0.3 yd, mean +0.4, p90 5.3 yd. Back-tee residual against the printed set: median -0.3 yd, inside 8 yd on 15 of 18 holes; against the rejected set: median -10.7 yd, inside 8 yd on 7 of 18. Summed over 18 holes the measured back tee spans 6824 yd (pad centroids) to 6916 yd (pad rear edges, where championship markers sit), an interval that CONTAINS the printed 6871 and misses the rejected 7240 by 324 yd. THE CONFOUND WAS TESTED AND REFUTED, and it is the crux: had the centrelines been drawn from a forward tee, every length would read short and the printed set would win by artifact. Each of the 18 centrelines starts at that hole's OWN back tee pad to within 0.1-3.7 m (median 0.4 m), and NOT ONE hole has any mapped tee pad behind its line start, so the lines are drawn from the tips. On the four divergent holes the rejected set needs a teeing ground 38, 113, 68 and 34 m behind the mapped back pad; none exists, and the LiDAR says what is there instead -- behind holes 5 and 17 the ground is mapped penalty area, and 113 m behind hole 10's pad the bare-earth returns fall 28 m on a 60-83% slope into a barranca, where no tee can be built. TWO HOLES MEASURE SHORT OF THE PRINTED CARD AND ARE NOT CLAIMED AS CONFIRMED. Hole 10 has only 4 pads mapped for 5 tee rows and its furthest-back pad measures 316-321 yd against a printed 338; its Blue row (317) is matched to 1 yd, so the Black pad is simply absent from the OSM extract rather than contradicted. Hole 18 measures 485-490 against a printed 503. Both are 3-vertex centrelines across a dogleg, which cuts a corner a measured yardage follows, and neither residual points at the rejected set -- on those same two holes the rejected set is a further 119-124 yd and 22-27 yd out. So the card is printed UNCHANGED, and holes 10 and 18 are recorded here as measured-short rather than as confirmed: a pro-shop reading of those two tee plates would settle them, and nothing in this book depends on the difference except the two numbers themselves.
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_LosAngeles_B23 (flown 2023-10-02), 0.4 m green surfaces at 10.4-15.3 ground pts/m^2; NAD83 UTM 11N

### Valley Hi Country Club
- **elevation** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_FEMALevee_D23 (2023, public domain)
- **geometry** — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); hole 17 centerline reconstructed to the unlabeled OSM green.
- **rating** — Ratings/slopes from the card (men's).
- **scorecard** — Official Valley Hi Country Club printed scorecard (valleyhicc.com/scorecard images ID 100301/100302): Black/White/Green/Gold per-hole yardages, par & men's handicap transcribed directly; all four tee totals verified (6997/6500/5868/5104). Ratings/slopes from the card (men's).
- **dem_source** — USGS 3DEP LiDAR CA_FEMALevee_D23 (2023), NAD83(2011) UTM10N + NAVD88; 0.4 m green surfaces at ~10-15 pts/m^2. Hole 17 centerline reconstructed to the unlabeled OSM green.
